messages:
Alex: quick Q — working through prefix caching behavior for the streaming text endpoint. how should we signal a cache hit to clients that stream? do we rely on headers only or send a control frame in the stream?
Maya: do we need both for backward compat? older clients just read headers. new streaming clients might miss initial headers if they only parse frames.
Ryan: proposal: keep backward-compatible headers (x-cache-hit: true/false) for non-streaming and for initial response headers. AND add an explicit streaming control event (JSON line) emitted before the first token for streaming responses. that way streaming clients can react immediately.
Jen: can you show an example of the header + stream event? makes it easier to review.
Ryan: sure — headers: 

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
x-cache-hit: true
x-cache-key: prefix:org123:abcd1234
cache-ttl: 3600
```

And streaming control event (first message in SSE or event-stream):

```
{"type":"cache","hit":true,"scope":"prefix","key":"prefix:org123:abcd1234","ttl":3600}
```

Then subsequent events contain token deltas. clients can ignore the control event if they only use headers.
Maya: what about partial hits? e.g., prefix matched but not whole prompt? We have cases where prefix cache returns tokens for first N tokens then runtime continues.
Ryan: for that we should include a field `partial:true` and `served_tokens:N` in the control frame. header `x-cache-hit` should still be `true` but add `x-cache-partial: true` and `x-cache-served-tokens: <N>` so non-streaming clients can inspect.
Alex: nice. how do we handle invalidation/backcompat? older clients might send prefix_key param name `prefix` while new ones use `prefix_key`.
Sam: easiest: server accepts both param names (deprecated alias) and returns a warning header `x-deprecated-prefix-param: prefix`. Additionally log metrics for deprecated usage.
Jen: invalidation race concerns — if an invalidation happens while a streaming response is in flight, what should the client expect?
Ryan: we should not retroactively change streamed tokens. If invalidation comes in mid-stream, the control frame still reflects the state at serve time. But we should emit an `invalidation_notice` as a separate control frame after the current chunk if the invalidation would affect subsequent requests. e.g.:

```
{"type":"invalidation","key":"prefix:org123:abcd1234","reason":"manual","at":"2024-11-02T14:23:00Z"}
```

This is informational for observability and client cache purging.
Maya: what about TTL derivation and namespace collisions? we should mandate client-supplied namespace or org id included in `cache_key` to avoid cross-tenant hits.
Alex: agreed — require `cache_namespace` param or prefix the key server-side with tenant id. document this.
ops-bot: rollout plan: Gate control-frame emission behind feature flag `streaming-cache-control-v1`. Default on for dedicated and private, opt-in for hosted beta. Telemetry: `cache_control_frame_emitted` metric.
Sam: i'll add a unit test matrix to cover header-only clients, streaming-with-control, partial hits, and invalidation frames. leaving a TODO for integration tests with client lib.
Jen: can someone add a short snippet to the API spec and a changelog note about the deprecated `prefix` param? also add a compatibility table.
Alex: Sam + Ryan take owner. Sam: tests + spec update. Ryan: implementation + rollout flag. I'll open a short RFC PR with examples and link here.
Sam: picking this up now — ping me on the PR when you have the draft.
Ryan: posted initial PR draft at https://rbw.internal/r/1234 — contains header/event examples and unit test plan. feedback welcome. :wave:
Alex: thanks all. this covers what I needed — will wait on the RFC and tests. :thumbsup:
